cim: Sam Garrison makes Amendment 3 a required course at Legislator University
cim_eredeti: Sam Garrison makes Amendment 3 a required course at Legislator University
szoveg_eredeti:
House Speaker Sam Garrison will require every House member to attend a class on Amendment 3 when the chamber holds Legislator University on Dec. 1 and 2.

Garrison laid out the two-day program in a Nov. 19 memo to members. It takes the place of House committee meetings that week, the House Office of Public Information told reporters Nov. 24. The Senate has no meetings on its interim calendar for that week.

Four classes are required of all members: one on the budget process and state revenues, one on Amendment 3, “Florida’s Digital Future,” and “Why You Want to Serve in My Silo: The Chairs Speak.” Attendance will be taken at every class.

Garrison singled out both Amendment 3 and artificial intelligence in his Organization Session speech.

The budget class opens the program at 9:30 a.m. Dec. 1. Amendment 3 follows at 10:30 a.m.

Garrison’s speech called the amendment “the biggest fiscal challenge our State has faced in a generation.” He told members “there is still no such thing as a free lunch.”

Gov. Ron DeSantis is pressing for a Special Session on the amendment before he leaves office. Garrison and Senate President Jim Boyd have said the work belongs in the Regular Session.

Garrison’s own list of open questions includes whether the same rules should apply to counties in very different fiscal shape. “I don’t think we necessarily know the answer to that yet,” WUSF’s Douglas Soule quoted him telling reporters after the speech.

“Florida’s Digital Future” is set for 10:30 a.m. Dec. 2. Garrison, who called himself “an analog guy in a digital world” in the speech, said artificial intelligence is the issue his term will be remembered for. He created a full Advanced Technology & Digital Security Committee with jurisdiction over AI and cybersecurity.

The chairs’ session closes the required list at 11:15 a.m. Garrison’s picks, public since Nov. 9, include Traci Koster at Appropriations and Jennifer Canady at the new Policy & Strategy Committee. His Nov. 5 memo on committee structure described him as “committed to making committee time meaningful.”

New members have a fifth required class, “The Toolkit: The Calendar, the Bill Analysis, and LEAGIS,” at 8 a.m. Dec. 2.

Returning members should also attend at least two of the 10 other classes, and new members at least three, the memo says. The list includes parliamentary procedure, PreK-20 governance, child welfare, transportation planning and spending, behavioral health, and workforce. One, “Distributed Power,” covers counties, municipalities, and special districts.

The House is also offering two tours of the chamber murals, each capped at 20 members. Christopher Still painted the 10 works. The murals trace to a 1999 commission under then-Speaker John Thrasher, the last Clay County lawmaker to hold the gavel before Garrison.

The program is in person only. District staff are not authorized to travel to Tallahassee for it. Members may travel starting Nov. 30, and the House will reimburse hotel rates up to $225 plus tax.

The classes are open to the media. They will not be broadcast on The Florida Channel, the Office of Public Information said.

Legislator University dates to 2016 and then-Speaker Richard Corcoran. Then-Speaker Jose Oliva also ran it in a week with no House committee meetings in 2018.

The next committee week on the interim calendar starts Jan. 4.

— Ed. note: This story was drafted with assistance from AI. Editorial judgment, sourcing, and final review were performed by Peter Schorsch and the Florida Politics editorial team.
